title: Accept native WebView container ownership
status: PREPARED after preserved failed connector attempt
question: Do two actual WebViews retain the native container selected by their captured scene and event date through navigation, detachment, rebinding and peer teardown?
source_audit: DDScriptMessageHandler reads message.webView.window.windowScene and body on the UI thread before enqueueing MessageEmitter.
MessageEmitter replaces or removes the private native scene key supplied by the browser; WebViewEventReceiver removes it before encoding.
Receiver resolves the cached native view before the corrected browser date, restricted to the captured scene and Replay-enabled views. Ambiguous source-less multi-scene history omits container.
WebViewEventReceiver writes AnyEncodable directly and bypasses the native RUM mapper. Native input guards and backend output must be distinguished.
D11 already accepts legacy single-scene fallback; do not reopen or conflate that compatibility gate with this two-container proof.
unit_contract: Defer A/B browser writes, insert newer native views before draining, and require original scene/date owners independently of process representative; include subsequent A navigation and rebinding.
Captured unavailable scene and absent scene under multiple retained scene owners omit container; private routing metadata never survives encoding.
MessageEmitter overwrites spoofed private scene metadata with actual captured scene, or removes it for nil; preserve all original browser fields.

native_contract.owners: After actual Replay enablement, create three manual native view occurrences scoped to actual scene identities; require independently mapped IDs and Replay flags before browser dispatch. Bind browser dates strictly after the corresponding native start and before subsequent native navigation.
native_contract.callback_evidence: A fixture WKUserContentController wrapper observes the real WKScriptMessage and forwards it synchronously to the original installed SDK handler. Persist exact browser ID/phase/run, WebView instance and actual window scene before any mutation. Do not replace SDK routing or claim the input observation is encoded output.
native_contract.guards: Distinct actual scenes and WebViews; current-run navigation readiness; B representative before original A emission; exact attachment or nil before every dispatch; same A instance across rebind; disable/remove A before peer B emission. Source payload contains a spoofed private scene key that must be overwritten/removed.
native_contract.limits: Two serial native scenes; controlled browser bridge payloads through real WebKit, not Browser SDK integration certification. Replay is a prerequisite for container IDs; no per-scene replay or physical coexistence acceptance.

backend_contract: Query the complete native RUM session with an independent count and every page: twelve unique views, six native plus six declared browser views.
Bind each browser ID/run/phase/source/url to its independently mapped native container ID, or exact absence for detached A; never derive expectation from backend owner labels.
Require native application/session replacement, container source ios when present, browser source, exact payload counts/version and no private routing metadata.
Require zero session actions, Resources, errors and crashes; reject foreign, stale, missing, extra or duplicated events.
workflow: Extend existing clean-install frozen-source runner; include WebViewTracking and SessionReplay source in identity. Link only existing repository products to owned probe project. Predeclare and freeze exact contract before native run; preserve every attempt.
